To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that

the agonist A23187, but not PMA, causes the loss of palmitoylated residues in the 32-38 kDa region of the gel, and this loss of palmitate occurs in the presence of the calpain inhibitor E64d, suggesting that it is mediated by calpain.
A23187 causes a loss of radio- activity associated with a palmitoylated 38 kDa protein and PMA causes a mobility shift of a palmitoy-lated 38 kDa platelet protein.
A23187 causes a calpain-induced loss of palmitate from a 38-kDa protein, and PMA causes a protein kinase C-mediated change in the electrophoretic properties of the same protein.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the identification of palmitoylated membrane proteins in activated platelets and with the effects of A23185 and PMA on these proteins.
the effects of agonists on the palmitate content of platelet proteins and their potential role in signal transduction.
the effect of A23187, PMA, and E64d on the palmitate modification of a 38 kDa protein and the role of calpain in these events.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that

the palmitoylation of proteins in platelets is a dynamic process, which is regulated by different agonists, and that calpain is involved in the regulation of this process in A23187-stimulated platelets.
calpain is activated in response to A23187 and that the palmitoylation of a 38 kDa protein is lost as a result of this calpain activity.
A23187 and/or PMA may induce the activation of calpains and that the activation of the protein kinase C pathway is required for the PMA-induced mobility shift of the protein.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
calpain is activated by both A23187 and Triton, but only A23187 leads to a proteolysis of palmitoylated membrane proteins.
calpain is involved in the proteolytic modification of palmitoylated 30-38-kDa protein(s), whereas protein kinase C may be involved in the palmitoylation of this/these protein(s) in intact platelets.
the palmitoylation of proteins in platelets may be involved in the signal transduction pathway of platelet activation.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the effects of A231 87 and PMA are different.
A23187 and calpain have a common effect on a 35 kDa protein that may be important for platelet activation.
A23187 and, possibly, PMA, can induce the proteolysis and the loss of label from a palmitoylated 30-38-kDa protein, possibly a protein kinase C isoform.
